Cohere Labs is Cohere's research lab that seeks to solve complex machine learning problems. We support fundamental research that explores the unknown, and are focused on creating more points of entry into machine learning research.

entity.name: Covenant AI
entity.description:
Covenant AI: Open Infrastructure for Frontier Model Development

Covenant AI is an independent research lab building the infrastructure for frontier AI training outside the walls of centralized compute. Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

The proof is Covenant72B, a 72-billion parameter model trained on 1.2 trillion tokens by coordinating 20+ independent compute providers over the public internet, with only 6% communication overhead. The methodology behind it, including our SparseLoCo optimizer, was peer-reviewed and accepted at NeurIPS 2025. Our gradient compression system, PULSE, runs in production inside Fireworks AI and powers Cursor's Composer 2, validated by engineers with no stake in the claim.

Our architecture spans the full model development pipeline. Templar handles distributed pre-training. Basilica operates the compute platform that researchers and labs run on. Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

That’s exactly what Jetty AI is for this new wave of artificial intelligence.

We’re a startup foundry designing, launching, and supporting high-impact AI ventures that center human wellbeing, safety, and progress.

At a time when most companies are racing to automate everything, we’re asking:
What should AI do for humanity?
We believe the answer lies in building responsibly, testing rigorously, and creating jobs — not just replacing them.

Jetty AI is an applied AI systems studio focused on helping startups and enterprises deploy production-grade AI.

We work with teams building copilots, agent workflows, retrieval systems, and memory-driven AI platforms that must operate reliably inside real environments with proprietary data.

Our work sits at the layer between experimentation and deployment.

We support companies designing and shipping:

• agentic workflow systems
• RAG and structured retrieval architectures
• temporal and persistent memory layers
• evaluation and safety pipelines
• private AI deployments and sovereign infrastructure
• enterprise copilots connected to internal systems

Jetty AI partners directly with founders and platform teams to accelerate architecture decisions, reduce deployment friction, and move AI from prototypes into production environments.

Alongside consulting engagements, we are building Thoth, a local-first runtime environment for agent workflows designed for organizations where sensitive data cannot leave their infrastructure.

Jetty AI operates as a small, deeply technical studio working across the US and India with a distributed engineering team focused on real-world AI deployment.

entity.name: Forithmus
entity.description:
Forithmus is building medical intelligence.

Our mission is to develop generalist AI systems that can understand medical images and support clinicians across complex diagnostic workflows. By learning from large-scale medical imaging data and radiology reports, our models aim to help physicians interpret medical images faster, more consistently, and at global scale.

We believe one of the most important contributions of artificial intelligence in healthcare will be making physicians dramatically more productive and extending medical expertise to places where it is scarce.

Achieving this requires moving beyond narrow point solutions toward generalist medical AI systems that more closely mirror how clinicians interpret images in real clinical practice.

To accelerate progress toward medical intelligence, Forithmus develops large-scale datasets, foundation models, and research infrastructure for medical imaging, while collaborating openly with the global research and clinical community.
